FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Hand Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production and General Engineering Division 
Council. 


This standard was first issued in 1976 and revised in 1991 based on ISO 3316 : 1975. This revision has been taken 
up to align with ISO 3316 : 2012 ‘Assembly tools for screws and nuts — Attachments for hand-operated square 
drive socket wrenches — Dimensions and tests”, to keep pace with the international practices. This standard is 
technically equivalent with ISO 3316 : 2012. Addition of sampling and certification clauses have been made in 
this standard. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded offin accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 7991 : 2016 


Indian Standard 


ATTACHMENTS FOR HAND OPERATED SQUARE 
DRIVE SOCKET WRENCHES — SPECIFICATION 


(Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements for attachments 
for hand operated square drive socket wrenches. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given below contain provisions, which,

of applying the most recent editions of the standards

3 NOMENCLATURE 


Nomenclature of hand operated square drive socket 
wrenches shall be as given in IS 6293.

4.6 Driving square shall be in accordance with IS 7214 
and shall have a minimum hardness of 382 HV ( = 39

5 MATERIAL 


Suitable steels meeting the requirements laid down in 
6 and 9 shall be used. 


Example — 40 Crl, T50Cr 1 V23 of IS 4367 


6 HARDNESS 


Hardness at any point of the attachments shall be 382 
HV minimum (= 39 HRC). 


7 SURFACE PROTECTION 


The wrenches may be protected against rust by plating 
with nickel-chromium or zinc or blackening by 
chemical process or by any other suitable process. 


8 SAMPLING 


8.1 Lot 


All the attachments of the same type and size in a 
consignment shall be grouped together to constitute a 
lot. 


8.2 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and 
the seller the procedure given in IS 2500 (Part 1) shall 
be followed for sampling inspection. 


8.2.1 For inspection of dimensions in single sampling 
plan corresponding to general inspection Level III and 
acceptable quality limit (AQL) of 2.5 percent given in 
Tables 1 and 2 of IS 2500 (Part 1) shall be followed. 


8.2.2 For torque testing, the single sampling plan 
corresponding to general inspection level II and AQL 
of 1.0 percent shall be followed. 


9 TORQUE TEST 


9.1 Method of Test 


The tool shall be placed in a female test square and the 
corresponding test torque as specified in relevant table 
shall be applied. The tool shall not be given any jerk or 
struck while testing. The load shall be gradually applied 
until the required test torque is reached. The test torque 
shall be calculated as the product of the magnitude of 
the load by the distance measured between the point of 
application of the load and the axis of the female test 
square. 


9.1.1 The nominal width across flats of the female test 
square shall be equal to the minimum dimension of the 
corresponding female square with a tolerance of H8. 
The female test square shall be hardened to not less 
than 595 HV (=55 HRC). 


9.1.2 A device in which the female test square can be 
rotated at a certain torque, determined with an accuracy 
of +2.5 percent, may also be used for the test. 


9.1.3 On completion of the test, the tool shall not show 
any permanent deformation or other damage which may 
influence usability. 


9.2 Application of Test Torque 


9.2.1 Adapter Socket Wrench, Extension Bar, and 
Universal Joint, Square Drive 


The test torque shall be applied using a driving part, 


IS 7991 : 2016 


the square of which has been treated for a minimum 
hardness of 595 HV (=55 HRC) and the width across 
flats dimension is equal to the maximum dimension of 
the corresponding male square with a tolerance h8. The 
universal joint shall be tested in the position in which 
the two squares are on the same axis. 


9.2.2 Square Drive Bit for Use with Spiral Ratchet 
Drives 


The end opposite to the square shall be fixed and the 
test torque shall be applied to that square. 


10 DESIGNATION 


10.1 An adapter socket wrench of Type A with male 
square size of 10 mm and female square size 12.5 mm 
shall be designated as: 


Adapter A IS 7991 — 10 x 12.5 


10.2 A universal joint square drive with nominal size 
of male and female square 12.5 mm shall be designated 
as: 


Universal Joint IS 7991 — 12.5 


10.3 An extension bar with male square size of 10 mm 
and female square size of 20 with nominal length 250 
mm shall be designated as: 


Extension Bar IS 7991 — 10 x 20 x 250 


10.4 A square drive bit for use with spiral ratchet drive 
of nominal size of male square 10 mm and shank 7 mm 
shall be designated as: 


Square Drive Bit IS 7991 — 10 x 7 


11 MARKING 


11.1 The attachments shall be marked with nominal size 
of square, manufacturer’s name or initials and 
recognized trade-mark. 


11.2 BIS Certification Marking 
The product may also be marked with standard mark. 


11.2.1 The use of Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


“BIS Catalogue” and “Standards : Monthly Additions”.
